title: The return of the sea eagle
text: The white-tailed eagle {{1}} driven to extinction in Britain {{2}} 1918, persecuted by shepherds and trophy collectors alike. {{3}} took until 1975 for the first Norwegian chicks to be released {{4}} the west coast of Scotland, and the birds, winged like barn doors, took another generation to feel at home. Over a hundred pairs {{5}} now raised young, and on Mull the sea eagle {{6}} licence to print money: wildlife tourists pour in, and islanders, {{7}} income from eagle-watching is now substantial, once shot the birds as thieves. Economists reckon an eagle pair to be worth more {{8}} the lambs it was once accused of taking — a calculation that has quietly settled one of conservation's oldest arguments.

gaps.hint: passive: the eagle ___ driven to extinction
gaps.explanation: Past passive with a singular subject: was driven.
'It took until X for Y' — the fixed time frame.
'Off the coast' — position in the sea near the coast.
Present perfect agreeing with the plural 'pairs': have raised.

gaps.hint: verb: Mull ___ become a licence to print money
gaps.explanation: Present perfect with a singular subject: has become.
'Whose' links the islanders to their income.
